hints: Separate the differential equation so all y-terms are on one side and the factor \(e^{-x}\) is on the other.
Integrate \(\int dy/(1+4y^2)\) by recognising the derivative of \(\tan^{-1}(2y)\), and integrate \(e^{-x}\).
Use \(x=1, y=0\) to determine the constant before applying tangent and isolating \(y\).
walkthrough:
State the given first-order differential equation:
$$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 + 4y^2}{\mathrm{e}^x}$$

Separate variables by dividing by $1 + 4y^2$ and multiplying by $dx$:
$$\dfrac{1}{1 + 4y^2}\,dy = \mathrm{e}^{-x}\,dx$$

Evaluate the left-hand integral using the standard result $\int \dfrac{1}{1 + u^2}\,du = \tan^{-1}(u)$ with $u = 2y$ (hence $du = 2\,dy$):
$$\int \dfrac{1}{1 + (2y)^2}\,dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{2}{1 + (2y)^2}\,dy = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2y)$$

Combine the two sides to obtain the general implicit solution:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2y) = -\mathrm{e}^{-x} + C$$

Use the initial condition $y = 0$ when $x = 1$ to determine the constant of integration $C$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2 \times 0) = -\mathrm{e}^{-1} + C$$
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(0) = -\mathrm{e}^{-1} + C$$
$$0 = -\mathrm{e}^{-1} + C \implies C = \mathrm{e}^{-1}$$

Substitute $C = \mathrm{e}^{-1}$ back into the implicit solution:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2y) = \mathrm{e}^{-1} - \mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Multiply both sides by $2$ to isolate the inverse tangent term:
$$\tan^{-1}(2y) = 2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x}$$

Apply the tangent function to both sides:
$$2y = \tan\left(2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right)$$

Divide by $2$ to obtain the explicit expression for $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$y = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\left(2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Solving Separable Differential Equations: Derives a term of the form \(\tan^{-1}(2y)\). Derives \(\frac12\tan^{-1}(2y)\). The final result is \(\displaystyle y=\frac12\tan(2e^{-1}-2e^{-x})\), or equivalent.

hints: Take the limit directly in the solution obtained in part (a).
As \(x\to\infty\), the term \(e^{-x}\) tends to zero.
Substitute that limiting value into the tangent expression for \(y\) and state the constant approached.
walkthrough:
Consider the explicit solution for $y$ found in part (a):
$$y = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\left(2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right)$$

Determine the behavior of the exponential term $\mathrm{e}^{-x}$ as $x \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} \mathrm{e}^{-x} = 0$$

Substitute this limit into the argument of the tangent function:
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} \left(2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2\mathrm{e}^{-x}\right) = 2\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 2(0) = 2\mathrm{e}^{-1}$$

Evaluate the limiting value of $y$:
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} y = \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\left(2\mathrm{e}^{-1}\right) \quad \left(\text{or } \dfrac{1}{2}\tan\left(\dfrac{2}{\mathrm{e}}\right) \approx 0.453\right)$$
